_comment: Relative plausibility priors over a pronunciation hypothesis's origin, used by hypothesis_scorer.py as LAMBDA * log_prior added to each candidate's length-normalized CTC log-likelihood. Unlike gop_config.py's old GLOBAL_PRIOR (which was derived from a real synthetic corpus), these are NOT data-derived - they encode an ordinal ranking from commonly-cited developmental phonology references: cluster reduction, stopping, fronting, gliding, and final consonant deletion are frequently documented as among the most common simplification processes in early childhood speech; devoicing/voicing and vowelization somewhat less so; backing and deaffrication are comparatively rare and often flagged as atypical when present. A data-driven candidate (an acoustic competitor with no matching documented process) gets the lowest prior: real acoustic evidence, but no independent linguistic reason to expect it. Both these values and LAMBDA (hypothesis_config.py) are starting points, meant to be tuned against eval/speechocean_train.jsonl (the dev split) - see eval/run_hypothesis_eval.py. Never trust them by construction; only keep changes that measurably improve dev numbers.
